sentences.text: How do you know your deviation card is still right?
You check it, and the best tool is one you met in lesson three: a range.
Line the boat up on a range, so the two marks are one above the other.
The chart gives you the range’s direction.
Compare that, as a magnetic direction, with what your compass reads.
The difference is your deviation on that heading.
You can also compare your compass with the GPS course over ground.
But only in calm water with no current, and it’s rougher.
Checking on all headings, and writing down the results, is called swinging ship.
And when should you check again?
Any time you install new electronics, or move gear near the compass.
A new stereo speaker can throw it off by ten degrees.
